title: Provider and Capability Maturity
readerIntent: Interpret capability and provider readiness honestly and understand the evidence required to promote it.
priorKnowledge: Understand capability ownership, provider adapters, testing, and deployment qualification.
owner: Owning capability/provider modules with repository governance and deployment evidence
summary: Maturity is an evidence-backed engineering status, not a marketing label: framework capability readiness, provider readiness, and a customer's production deployment qualification are separate decisions.

sections.heading: Levels
items: Production-ready capability: reusable contract, implementation, configuration/extension path, deterministic tests, operations, security, and documentation are ready for project use after project/deployment qualification.
Guarded provider: implemented adapter/runtime exists, but use requires explicit configuration, secrets, topology, isolation, live integration/release tests, and operational ownership.
Sample or reference: demonstrates behavior, seeds local development, or proves structure; it is not customer production policy.
Placeholder or scaffold: boundary exists but required implementation, provider capabilities, health, tests, or operations are incomplete; keep inactive or fail closed.
Parked future capability: need is recorded outside runtime documentation and intentionally deferred; do not expose or claim it as implemented.

sections.heading: Three independent questions
items: Is the provider-neutral Nodics capability implemented and governed?
Is the selected provider adapter complete and qualified for its claimed guarantees?
Has this customer deployment configured and tested the capability/provider in its actual topology, scale, security, data, recovery, and compliance context?
A production-ready capability may use a guarded provider; neither label certifies a specific cloud/customer deployment automatically.

sections.heading: Current important boundaries
items: NodeCache is sample/reference for local or single-process behavior; it is not strict distributed state.
Redis cache is guarded and requires configured live release evidence; strict distributed authentication depends on qualified atomic shared behavior.
Hazelcast cache remains placeholder/scaffold until a real adapter proves distributed operations, atomic behavior where claimed, health, lifecycle, and live tests.

MongoDB is guarded for production deployment and requires tenant databases, secrets, indexes, backup/restore, capacity, and live validation; Cassandra and elastic database adapters remain scaffold boundaries unless their evidence changes.
Elasticsearch search and Kafka messaging are guarded providers requiring endpoints/topology, isolation/security, health, recovery, capacity, upgrade, and live tests.
ActiveMQ remains a messaging provider scaffold until implementation and live evidence are complete.
CronJob and Workflow are implemented capabilities, while every customer job/workflow still owns idempotency, process rules, topology, failure, and release tests.
MonoServer and Startio are local/reference validation structures; modular/customer production topology requires independent deployment qualification.

sections.heading: Promotion evidence
items: Named owner, neutral/provider boundary, supported versions, configuration and later-layer override path, secrets/endpoints, tenant/isolation model, data flow, lifecycle, health/readiness, diagnostics, capacity, failure/retry/recovery, backup/restore, migration/upgrade/rollback, and security threat model.
Positive, negative, boundary, contract, integration, customization, live-provider, outage, recovery, performance/load, topology, security, upgrade, and regression tests.
Current module README, canonical user/developer/operator documentation, generated context, examples, runbooks, and release gate.
Evidence date, environment, exact versions/commands/results, limitations, residual risks, approver, and requalification trigger.

sections.heading: Governance rules
items: Change maturity only when owned evidence changes; never promote from a scaffold, unit test, local success, installed provider, or configuration flag alone.
A regression, unsupported version, missing owner, failed live gate, unsafe fallback, or absent recovery evidence may demote a capability/provider.
Keep unavailable behavior inactive or fail closed and state the missing work explicitly.
AI tools and developers must consult effective module configuration, current tests, provider health, and this register before recommending a production design.
Customer deployment approval remains the customer's shared-responsibility decision even when framework and provider evidence pass.
